core.title: Bind at least one test to an acceptance of every feature that owns DESIRED OUTCOMES
core.given: A plan feature owns one or more DESIRED OUTCOMES (behaviours declared for it in the plan).
core.when: the topology coverage check verifies whether any test is bound to one of that feature's acceptances.
core.then: At least one test is bound to one of the feature's acceptances.
prefer: Add a test beneath the feature, bound to one of its acceptances.
avoid: Leaving declared feature behaviour (DESIRED OUTCOMES) with no test bound to any of its acceptances.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the stack-wide excluded list; the exact classification is owned by the check).
core.why: Behaviour declared and never tested is a silent gap.
evidence: The topology coverage check reports no feature that owns DESIRED OUTCOMES without at least one test bound to one of its acceptances.
A failing fixture (a feature with DESIRED OUTCOMES and no bound test) is flagged by the stack's convention check.
verification: The check scans the roots declared in the profile (plan, test, e2e and source roots) plus the repository root configuration; a change to the root configuration can change which files are scanned.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; roots.excluded is one stack-wide list and the exact exclusion classification is deferred to the check.
Coverage is satisfied by any scanned test bound to one of the feature's acceptances, wherever it is placed; placement beneath the feature is the recommended fix, not a condition of this rule.

values: a feature that owns DESIRED OUTCOMES has no test bound to any of its acceptances
feature or DESIRED OUTCOME added to the plan
test bound to a feature acceptance removed or unbound
scanned root changed in the repository root configuration

fires: A plan feature declares DESIRED OUTCOMES but no test anywhere in the scanned files is bound to any of its acceptances.
The only test bound to a feature's acceptance (unit or end-to-end) is deleted or unbound, leaving the feature's DESIRED OUTCOMES with no bound test.
A scanned root or the repository root configuration is changed so that no scanned test bound to a feature's acceptances remains (e.g. the only bound tests now fall outside every scanned root).
doesNotFire: A feature that owns no DESIRED OUTCOMES has no tests.
A feature with DESIRED OUTCOMES has at least one test bound to one of its acceptances, wherever that test is placed.
Files inside vendored or generated trees (never scanned).

profileRequirements.meaning: Where plan artifacts (features and their DESIRED_OUTCOMES/acceptances) live; parsed to find features owning DESIRED OUTCOMES and their acceptances.
Root of production source; also scanned, because a test bound to an acceptance may live inside it.
Root of unit and acceptance tests when they live outside the source tree; scanned for tests bound to acceptances.
Root of end-to-end tests; scanned for tests bound to acceptances.
The repository file that declares the scanned roots; changing it can change which files are scanned.
Which roots a repository-wide run of this check scans.
profileRequirements.bunValue: all four topology roots: plan_root, test_root, e2e_root, source_root

profileRequirements.meaning: Vendored and generated trees that are never scanned (one stack-wide list; the exact classification is owned by the check).

bunOnly.text: The atdd_topology validator reports no feature that owns DESIRED OUTCOMES without at least one test bound to one of its acceptances.
bunOnly.reason: The validator id (atdd_topology) names this stack's realization of the check; the core states the check generically.

bunOnly.text: A failing fixture (feature with DESIRED OUTCOMES, no bound test) is flagged by the package guard.
bunOnly.reason: 'Package guard' is ATDD-Bun's own-gates machinery (the package_rule term); the core names the stack's convention check generically.
Finding ids of this single rule are realization details; the core describes the finding neutrally and lets verification name the check generically.

bunOnly.text: Source statement: "Package rule, strict." (a rule of this package's own gates, realized by a package guard)
bunOnly.reason: The package_rule framing ('this package's own gates, package guard') is ATDD-Bun-specific; the severity and strict disposition themselves are kept in core verification.

classification.note: Already neutral: DESIRED OUTCOME is the ATDD plan-artifact term, kept with its gloss.
'topology gate' generalized to 'topology coverage check'; no stack named.
The single obligation, already stack-neutral; kept verbatim.
Role-level fix; 'beneath the feature' names no path or stack.
The exception is neutral (never-scanned trees); the concrete list (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) is the stack-wide excluded list, with the exact classification deferred to the check.
Neutralized to 'the topology coverage check reports...'; the validator id atdd_topology stays with the realization.
Neutralized to 'the stack's convention check'; the package-guard framing stays with the realization.
Roots come from the profile (plan/test/e2e/source roots and the root configuration file); the atdd-bun.yaml key names and defaults are the Bun profile values.
Check scope only: never-scanned vendored/generated trees, one stack-wide list.
Scope clarification: binding, not placement, satisfies coverage; prevents strengthening the obligation into a placement rule.
Per-rule severity (3) and disposition (strict) belong to core verification; the 'Package rule' source framing is ATDD-Bun-specific.
The path globs become a file_kind fact over the scanned kinds; each concrete glob/root and the config file are the profile's root values, and the filtered trees are roots.excluded.
Finding fact kept neutrally (feature with DESIRED OUTCOMES, no bound test anywhere; location not part of the finding); the finding slug is a realization id.
Change values neutral; 'topology root changed in atdd-bun.yaml' becomes 'scanned root changed in the repository root configuration' (roots.config).

neutralityNotes: DESIRED OUTCOME is kept as the ATDD plan-artifact term (glossed as behaviours declared for the feature in the plan), matching the vocabulary's plan_artifact/urn.desired-outcome usage. The core speaks of a test 'bound' to an acceptance; the concrete binding syntax is the profile key urn.binding.acceptance, which the frozen sidecar does not spell out (the validator resolves bindings internally), so no Bun value is recorded for it here. The 'package rule / package guard' framing and the validator/finding ids are ATDD-Bun realization details kept in bunOnly. Nothing else required a stack-specific term.
